An English crib of the Latin text, semi-literal, made for this database in 2026 with Claude, a large language model (LLM) made by Anthropic. It keeps close to the wording of the original and uses the established English of Anglo-Latin legal, liturgical and canon-law formulae. It is an aid to reading the original, not a published translation. Square brackets mark Liebermann’s additions to the text or, now and then, words supplied for the sense; “[?]” marks a doubtful reading

div.head: ECf 24.3
div.ab: Et si dominus, in cuius terra inuentum est, non habet consuetudines suas, scilicet sache et sochne, omnia liberabit prefecto hundredi, si habere uoluerit, cum bonis testibus.
div.note: Liebermann’s text transcribed from Gesetze I p. 650 (November 2026): read from the page images and checked against the scan’s own text layer, differences settled against the page.

note.seg: private Gerichtsbarkeit, hier im Gegensatz zu hundred; doch besass mancher Baron eine Hundertschaft ganz
private jurisdiction, here in contrast to hundred; but many a baron possessed a whole hundred

div.ab: And if the lord in whose land it was found does not have his customs, namely sake and soke, he shall deliver everything to the reeve of the hundred, if he wishes to have it, with good witnesses.
